alt.en: A printed journal page headed "A PRAYER": a short paragraph about the manuscripts, then ten numbered two-line stanzas in Irish beginning "Rob tu mo bhoile, a Comdi cride", with footnotes below.
alt.es: Una página impresa de revista con el título "A PRAYER": un párrafo breve sobre los manuscritos y luego diez estrofas numeradas de dos versos en irlandés, que empiezan "Rob tu mo bhoile, a Comdi cride", con notas al pie.

caption.en: Page 89 of the journal Ériu, vol. 2 (Dublin, 1905): Mary Byrne's edition of the Irish poem, which she called "A Prayer", taken from Royal Irish Academy manuscript 23 N 10, pages 95 and 96.
caption.es: La página 89 de la revista Ériu, vol. 2 (Dublín, 1905): la edición de Mary Byrne del poema irlandés, que ella tituló "A Prayer" (Una oración), tomada del manuscrito 23 N 10 de la Real Academia Irlandesa, páginas 95 y 96.

source: M. E. Byrne, "A Prayer", Ériu: The Journal of the School of Irish Learning, vol. 2 (Dublin, 1905), p. 89
callNumber: Internet Archive eriu_1905_2, image n92 (printed page 89)
licenceEvidence: Published Dublin 1905; Mary E. Byrne died 1931 (the journal's editors, Kuno Meyer and John Strachan, died 1919 and 1907). Public domain in the US (published before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70 ended 2001). Scan of a flat page.

alt.en: A printed book page headed "A PRAYER": eight rhyming couplets beginning "Be Thou my Vision, O Lord of my heart", page number 119 at the foot, with faint print showing through from the other side.
alt.es: Una página de libro impresa con el título "A PRAYER": ocho pareados que riman, empezando por "Be Thou my Vision, O Lord of my heart", con el número de página 119 al pie y letras tenues que se transparentan desde el reverso.

caption.en: Page 119 of Eleanor Hull's The Poem-Book of the Gael (London, 1912): the first eight of the twelve couplets she made from Byrne's prose, the words hymnals sing, with changes.
caption.es: La página 119 de The Poem-Book of the Gael, de Eleanor Hull (Londres, 1912): los ocho primeros de los doce pareados que hizo a partir de la prosa de Byrne, la letra que, con cambios, cantan los himnarios.

source: Eleanor Hull, ed., The Poem-Book of the Gael (London: Chatto & Windus, 1912), "A Prayer", p. 119
library: University of Toronto, Robarts Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: AER-2609; Internet Archive poembookofgaeltr00hulluoft, image n160 (printed page 119)
licenceEvidence: Published London 1912; Eleanor Hull died 1935 (archive.org record: "Hull, Eleanor, 1860-1935"; possible-copyright-status "NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT"). Public domain in the US (published before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70 ended 2005). Scan of a flat page.
credit: University of Toronto, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed music heading, "THE JOYCE COLLECTION", page 151, then "323. WITH MY LOVE ON THE ROAD." above two lines of a tune in 3/4 time with one flat, with no words.
alt.es: Un encabezado de música impresa, "THE JOYCE COLLECTION", página 151, y debajo "323. WITH MY LOVE ON THE ROAD." sobre dos pentagramas de una melodía en 3/4 con un bemol, sin letra.

caption.en: No. 323, "With my love on the road", in P. W. Joyce's Old Irish Folk Music and Songs (1909): the earliest known printing of the tune later called SLANE.
caption.es: El n.º 323, "With my love on the road" (Con mi amor por el camino), en Old Irish Folk Music and Songs de P. W. Joyce (1909): la primera impresión conocida de la melodía que más tarde se llamó SLANE.

source: P. W. Joyce, ed., Old Irish Folk Music and Songs (London: Longmans, Green; Dublin: Hodges, Figgis, 1909), No. 323, "With my love on the road", p. 151
library: University of Toronto, Kelly Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: 09014968; Internet Archive oldirishfolkmusi00royauoft, image n192 (printed page 151)
licenceEvidence: Published London and Dublin 1909; editor P. W. Joyce died 1914 (archive.org record: "Joyce, P. W. (Patrick Weston), 1827-1914"; possible-copyright-status "NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT"); the tune is traditional. Public domain in the US (published before 1931), the EU and Israel (life plus 70 ended 1984). Scan of a flat page, cropped to No. 323.
